title: Gecko Robotics, Anduril team up for new Baltimore County shipyard
key_facts: Gecko Robotics announced on 8 Oct 2026 it will deploy its inspection robots and AI software at Anduril facilities.
Anduril is preparing Arsenal-2, a Baltimore County, Maryland shipyard to make submarine parts.
On Tuesday Anduril and the White House announced a $6.6 billion investment: $3.7 billion private and up to $2.9 billion from the Navy.
Initial operations at Arsenal-2 are targeted for 2030.
Gecko's non-destructive testing will inspect welds and other parts and build a 'digital thread' of maintenance data; it is already used at Anduril's Orange County, California protofactory.
Industry has struggled to meet the Navy's goal of two Virginia-class submarines a year.
In March the Navy awarded Gecko a contract of up to $71 million over five years for hull-crawling robots.
quote_evidence: Gecko Robotics will deploy its robotics and AI software at Anduril facilities, the company announced today, as Anduril prepares to launch its new Arsenal-2 shipyard in Baltimore County, Md., to manufacture submarine parts.

Currently, Anduril is preparing for the facility to launch initial operations in 2030, and plans to expand production from basic submarine parts into more complex sections of the vessel, like the bow.
Anduril’s shipyard announcement comes as industry has struggled to meet the Navy’s production goal of two Virginia-class submarine deliveries annually.
why_it_matters_hint: Inspection robots are being built into the plan to make submarine parts faster.
notes: Both companies announced; the shipyard is not yet permitted or built.
